items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: my engineer Hank Cicalo, well there were other engineers but primarily he’s the one that comes to mind because I did L.A. Express, New York Connection, all that stuff with him.

ctx.x: Well right now of course I’m doing some gratis work. Of course I’ve got my podcast, I’ve got a radio show on KJZZ which is the Southern California jazz station, I’ve got a weekly jazz show there called “Hang Time with Tom Scott.” I’m doing of course I’ve done a lot of — I got on Tik Tok at the recommendation of the guy who is now my producer in Connecticut actually, and so I’ve got a whole series of Tik Toks where they’re sort of two part Tik Toks. The first one is where I play that portion of a record where I’ve…

is a wonderful ukulele player in Hawaii and we did a whole album with her, some jazz tunes, some folky, folkish kind of tunes, even one classical tune. We did the Faure “Pavane” kind of in the style of a Bill Evans with a symphony orchestra record. And except for her playing and a couple of jazz soloists that I got on the record, Arturo Sandoval, Ray Parker and Michael McDonald did a whole bunch of vocals on one of his tunes. But the rest was all me: drums and bass and keyboards and strings and everything, and…

Let me just wrap up, I forgot to ask about Paul McCartney, who over the years definitely knew what he wanted. I think of the “Penny Lane” trumpet solo and apparently how he vocalized it and had George Martin write it down.

items.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022
items.q: I got into a thing a couple of times with Tom Scott but what we actually did was it was a transition from one tune to another tune

ctx.x: Yeah, I know. It’s just this — I’ve always loved that moment and I’m curious which studio cat played that.

I’ll tell you the things — I got into a thing a couple of times with Tom Scott but what we actually did was it was a transition from one tune to another tune where you could just do it with two pots. But there were a couple of times where Tom wanted to keep the thing going a little longer so you had the cut that you normally would make, this is not going to work. We would do these really surgical things. You’d take, instead of Editall block, which is really six inches, you take two pieces of masking tape and put…
Yeah he told me that you would do mixes where you had sixteen faders and he had sixteen and I can almost picture how that, “No, no, not yet, don’t push that up yet.”
